title: Add retry logic to embeddings and decouple metadata from chunks
note: Establishes the convention: never let a vector index and its metadata sidecar fall out of lockstep.

title: Add a retryable fetch helper for flaky external calls
note: Establishes the convention: external/flaky calls must retry with exponential backoff.

title: Add a per-key cache writer instead of one shared file
note: Establishes the convention: persist results keyed by id, not round-tripped through one shared file.

title: Validate required config eagerly at load time
note: Establishes the convention: validate required config eagerly and fail fast with a clear error.

title: Add a separate vector index over PR authors' past explanations
note: Pushes to metadata before confirming the paired vector was added -- same bug class as PR #1.

title: Add a helper to fetch a PR's labels
note: A single external GitHub API call with zero retry logic.

title: Add a rolling summary of delivered findings
note: Writes every call's findings to one shared data/processed/summary.json -- same race condition shape as the original findings.json bug.

title: Add configurable prompt tone setting
note: Reads process.env.PROMPT_TONE deep inside a function with no upfront check -- crashes confusingly on .toUpperCase() if unset, instead of failing fast.

title: Add a small numeric clamp helper
note: Trivial, unrelated utility -- nothing to flag. Replaces PR #10 (see eval/README.md: PR #10 accidentally duplicated PR #3's inline sleep() helper, which the bot correctly flagged as a real DRY violation -- not a model failure, a test-data flaw).

title: Add a small date-formatting helper for delivery timestamps
note: Trivial, unrelated utility -- nothing to flag.

title: Add a separate vector index over historical PR titles
note: Deliberately similar in shape to PR #1/#6 (another small index builder) but implements the convention correctly -- tests for false positives on code that merely looks similar.

title: Add a small helper to validate required params up front
note: Deliberately similar in spirit to PR #5/#9 (config/param validation) but implements the convention correctly -- another false-positive check.
